# Our Git workflow strategy {.unnumbered}

**Repository.** Zoé created the public repository `IEAP-Series03-RStudio` on her GitHub
account and added Alexis and Albatoul as collaborators. Her first two commits set up the
project (README, LICENSE, `.gitignore`, RStudio project, master document, references and
data). After that, nobody committed directly on `main`: it only received merges.

**One file per person.** The master document only contains the header and the `include`
lines. Each question lives in its own file in `sections/`, and each file has one owner, so
we never edit the same lines and we never had a merge conflict.

| Member | Questions | File | Branch |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Zoé SAUGE | 1.1, 1.2 | `_01-question.qmd` | `1.1Think` |
| Alexis LAGARDE | 1.3 | `_02-data-anova.qmd` | `1.2-data-anova` |
| Albatoul AHMAD | 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 | `_03-regression-graph.qmd` | `1.4-1.6-regression-graph` |
| Zoé SAUGE | 1.7 | `_04-discussion.qmd` | `1.7-discussion` |
| Alexis LAGARDE | Git workflow | `_05-git-workflow.qmd` | `git-challenges` |
| Everyone | challenges, sources, checklist | `_06-challenges-checklist.qmd` | `git-challenges` |

**Branches and pull requests.** Each part was developed on its own branch, created from an
up-to-date `main`, and merged back through a pull request on GitHub.

**Order of the merges.** The questions depend on each other: the regression (1.4) uses the
participant means `mt` created in 1.3, the figure (1.5–1.6) uses the regression, and the
discussion (1.7) uses `regression_models`, `mt_summary` and the ANOVA table. The pull
requests were therefore merged in the order of the questions: `1.1Think` (#1), then
`1.2-data-anova` (#2), then `1.4-1.6-regression-graph`, then `1.7-discussion`. Before
starting a new branch, each member pulled `main`.
